hook.text: Sauerkraut requires two ingredients: cabbage and salt. Bacteria already on the cabbage do the rest.

buildup.text: Salt suppresses spoilage bacteria while Lactobacillus—naturally present on vegetables—thrives and produces lactic acid.

discovery.text: As pH drops below 4.6, pathogens die. The food is self-preserving—bacteria create a hostile environment for competitors.

twist.text: Korean families traditionally buried kimchi jars underground. Soil temperature (~15°C) provides natural, slow fermentation.

climax.text: Lacto-fermented foods contain live bacteria, B vitamins, and enhanced bioavailability of minerals—more nutritious than raw.

punchline.text: Salt plus time plus wild bacteria. Nature's original preservation system.

quiz.question: What makes lacto-fermented foods self-preserving?
options: Lactic acid bacteria lower pH, creating hostile conditions for pathogens
